verdict.rationale: ClickHouse ships an official MCP server (mcp-clickhouse) that lets an AI agent run SQL against ClickHouse via a keyless JSON-RPC handshake, and points to an official Agent Skills repo for coding-agent integration, showing real agent-delegated SQL execution. However, the evidence never documents that the MCP tools are scoped to distinguish read-only queries from destructive/DDL operations (no mention of a read-only mode, permission tiers, or tool-level safety separation). Missing for 10: explicit documentation of read-only vs destructive tool scoping, evidence of permission/role enforcement at the tool level, and independent confirmation that destructive actions are gated or blocked.
